rounds.notes:
When playing Stadium as Tracer, there are three truths: building a strong econ wins games, you can’t farm Stadium Cash if you’re dead, and you die very easily. With that in mind, we’re going to play with the mindset of a gnat - but a ***smart gnat***. Your starting items will make you just enough of a threat to force enemies to turn around, but unless you’re going in with full cooldowns or taking a 1v1 against someone already half health, there’s a good chance you die. And **we do not want to die**. Play safe, harass the backline, and chip away at their mental. You’ll hit a power spike in round 3 that upgrades you from gnat to mosquito, but until then, patience is key.

---

First power we pick [Quantum Clip](item_3a108115-ec6e-4b98-8074-1b015cf535f1). This is going to give us a massive edge in any early 1v1’s we end up taking, especially against other Tracers who won’t be expecting you to have the extra 10 bullets or the extra 10% life steal.

You’ll see a lot of builds recommend [Foresight](item_f4163ce1-8f80-43ca-85d4-39812084400f) here instead. Let’s address that. Tracer isn’t supposed to need auto-aim - if you’re close enough to play her properly, you should be landing your shots pretty easily. When I see someone pick [Foresight](item_f4163ce1-8f80-43ca-85d4-39812084400f) this early, I immediately smell fear. It tells me they don’t trust their mechanics, and that means they’re already playing from behind. We’re not doing that. We’re going to win fights on positioning, timing, and precision, not training wheels. Freeing up that power slot sets us up better for the long game. I know that might sound intimidating, but it’s really not - we just like to pretend it is so our ego feels good.

---

The gameplay loop is Shoot > Reload > Blink during Reload > Shoot.

---

Again, the goal of this round is to stay alive, so if you realize you aren’t going to win the fight, time to blink out, find a health pack, and blink back in.  For first items we are grabbing some Weapon Power, some Weapon Lifesteal (to stack on what we are going to be carrying with [Quantum Clip](item_3a108115-ec6e-4b98-8074-1b015cf535f1)), and then a survival item. I typically go with [First Aid Kit](item_0172eaaa-1902-44a3-b989-d12f0f7301da), but feel free to swap this out for [Ballistic Buffer](item_40146dd3-a8cb-40ca-8917-c430bfa2be0e) if you are going up against some hitscans who are going to poke you down.  Turn their backline into your frontline, tickle the supports, save a blink (always) to get out, and farm away.

round_upgrades.notes: Use this if you are worried about getting poked down from a distance (Ash/Soldier/Cassidy/Freja)

rounds.notes:
This round we start to build up our survivability. Typically we are up against weapon damage so I pick up [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09), but alternatively, if you notice they are building mostly ability power swap this out for [Reinforced Titanium](item_8ebaa7db-aedf-48ed-adc1-318cb46a3214).

If the enemy team has a mix of heroes building ability and weapon power, buy both. The main goal here is to farm cash and the most consistent way to do that is staying alive.

---

After our survivability item(s) we fill out our items with whatever green items we can. Usually I make sure to have [Technoleech](item_cb7fd8bf-bdcc-439a-ad35-372f24a027a8) and [Compensator](item_2a354f80-610c-4661-9bdd-8960ae1a60b0) following that up with [Weapon Grease](item_961ae72f-434f-406b-a89b-ab8efec806bf) if I have any cash left over. Usually I found this is about all I can afford round 2 but if you find yourself unusually flush, I would start to pivot towards more damage with any additional items.

We are still going to explode if someone looks at us the wrong way this round, so the best you can do is bob and weave. You want to be a constant presence in their backline but never in the same place long enough to get punished for it. You're not going to get many kills but you ***are*** going to farm a lot of cash and you'll be helping your team by splitting their attention.

Pick this up *in lieu* of Crusader Hydraulics if the enemy team is building mostly ability power. 

Pick this up *with* Crusader Hydraulics if the enemy team has a mix of ability and weapon damage builds.
Use this if you are worried about getting poked down from a distance (Ash/Soldier/Cassidy/Freja)

rounds.notes:
Alright, we’ve now hit mosquito. Looking at our second power, we’re going to start branching into a few different builds here depending on how the last two rounds went:

If you’ve been playing like a smart gnat and finding success, congrats - we’re taking [T.Racer](item_996e13d5-9521-4312-944f-d672f528776b) because we’re here to play mind games. Beyond the obvious benefit of extra blink distance, you’ll be surprised how much harder this makes you to track - especially for experienced Overwatch players. Muscle memory betrays enemy hitscans who expect you to appear 3 meters closer than you actually do, and that adjustment is harder than you’d think. It’ll take some getting used to on your end too, but the third-person perspective helps a lot with learning the new blink spacing. Picking this power first ensures you’ll have plenty of time to acclimate. At worst, spend a bit of time in the Stadium practice range. Sure, you’ll run into a handful of Cassidys or Soldiers who figure it out and swap into auto-targeting builds, but by the time they do, you should already have the survivability to deal with it.

For the above ***“Good Noodle”*** build, we’re going to lean a bit more into survivability with [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c). This will help you take advantage of the large shield pool you’ve built with [Vishkar Condensor](item_086a91da-b65d-4047-8fc7-28a992078b1d). Hang onto the two previous blue items and fill out whatever you can with green items.

***“Good Noodle”***

**Core Items:** [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c); [Vishkar Condensor](item_086a91da-b65d-4047-8fc7-28a992078b1d); [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09) (or [Reinforced Titanium](item_8ebaa7db-aedf-48ed-adc1-318cb46a3214)).

**New Items:** Fill the remaining slots with any green items you can afford. At this point we’re focusing on keeping that shield pool strong and ensuring we can keep harassing without dying. If you’ve been playing well, this setup lets you stay in fights longer and pressure their backline more consistently.

---

If you’ve been playing like a smart gnat but aren’t getting much value for the team - specifically if you’re struggling against ridiculous mobility heroes (and really, who would even pick a high-mobility hero in this mode… cringe) - then we’re going with [Foresight](item_f4163ce1-8f80-43ca-85d4-39812084400f). I know we talked a big game in round one about not needing auto-aim, but we’re going to forget that now. This mobility-based backline is clearly hacking and we have no choice.

For this ***“LowElo, I Think We’re Gonna Have to Kill This Guy”*** build, we’re going to sacrifice some survivability and grab [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182) and [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66). Any high-mobility characters we’re building for will almost certainly be above the 3-meter trigger range we need to proc [Stratosphere Beacon], and combined with the extra fire rate and auto-targeting from [Foresight] and [Shieldbuster], we should have a much easier time reminding them who the only mobility hero allowed in this lobby is… (it’s you).

***“LowElo, I Think We’re Gonna Have to Kill This Guy”***

![Image](https://i.imgur.com/ViV1qdF.jpeg)

**Core Items:** [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182); [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66).

**New Items:** The focus here is on punishing high-mobility heroes and shutting down escape attempts. If you find you’re still struggling to land shots or finish off targets, consider [Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a) for added weapon control or [Aftermarket Firing Pin](item_2485b212-b286-42d0-a2bd-20eb4396b054) if you’re tight on cash.

---

If you’ve been playing like a smart gnat but keep dying to burst damage (which should be the only thing killing you if you’re playing correctly), we now break into two different build paths:

•	If you’re dying to one-shot hitscans (Cassidy, Ashe), take [Auto Recall](item_ae3dbebf-c306-4408-b698-6f666ace0a7c). Pair this with [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c) and [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09). Spend any extra Stadium Cash on [Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a) if you can afford it, or [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66) if you’re short. If neither is an option, that’s okay - you’re doing great, sweetie. Just fill in with any other green items you can afford. We’ll call this build path ***“Nah, He’s Soft-Locking for Sure.”***

***“Nah, He’s Soft-Locking for Sure” (Hitscan one-shots)***

**Core Items:** [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c); [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09).

**New Items:** [Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a) if you can afford it, or [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66) if you need a cheaper option. If neither is viable, round things out with [Aftermarket Firing Pin](item_2485b212-b286-42d0-a2bd-20eb4396b054), [Compensator](item_2a354f80-610c-4661-9bdd-8960ae1a60b0), or [Weapon Grease](item_961ae72f-434f-406b-a89b-ab8efec806bf). Your main goal here is to dance around their DPS and be a distraction, but a *survivable* distraction.

•	If you’re dying to one-shot projectiles (Pharah, Junkrat, Juno), take [Bullet Time](item_6840382c-ae92-491a-b70c-b49f3a76003a). We’re still focused on survivability with [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c). If you’re facing a Junkrat here, keep the rest of your survival items and play around your recall - only dive him if recall is off cooldown. If it’s a Pharah… ew. Let’s also grab [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182) so we’re a bit more threatening earlier. If needed, you can sell [Vishkar Condensor](item_086a91da-b65d-4047-8fc7-28a992078b1d) to afford this (don’t worry, we’ll rebuild our shield size with other items). We’ll call this path **“Pharmerc-udical Solutions.”** (Sure, it’s a stretch - but you try coming up with these.)

***“Pharmerc-udical Solutions” (Projectile one-shots)***

**Core Items:** [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c); [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182) (sell [Vishkar Condensor](item_086a91da-b65d-4047-8fc7-28a992078b1d) if needed).

**New Items:** If you’re playing around projectile spam (especially Junkrat), you’ll want to maximize uptime and survivability — focus any extra Stadium Cash on green items like [Aftermarket Firing Pin](item_2485b212-b286-42d0-a2bd-20eb4396b054) or [Compensator](item_2a354f80-610c-4661-9bdd-8960ae1a60b0). The plan here is to harass safely and dive only when recall is available.

---

If you haven’t been playing like a smart gnat… come on, man. We talked about this. Remember: living = strong econ, strong econ = win. We want to win (in case I hadn’t covered that already). Drink some water, sit up straight, lock in, and let’s get back on track, champ. ***forehead kiss***

In the optional items, you’ll start seeing situational picks I’ve swapped in for each of these build paths - I’ve labeled them as such in the item notes, along with options for when you’ve got excess Stadium Cash (yay!). For situational swaps, trust your gut and keep the core goal in mind: always stay alive. If you’re alive, you’re drawing attention, farming cash, and driving supports insane - in short, you’re bringing value to the team.

rounds.notes:
So… we didn’t mercy rule them this game. Well, that’s too bad for them - now we get to start having some real fun.

For items, we’re grabbing [Vanadium Injection](item_57953fbc-11ff-4e92-9928-fc59b7be668f). Which means: no more ult. I know, I know… tragic. Here’s the thing - we all want to be Kabaji, but let’s be realistic. The cooldown reduction, bonus health, attack speed, and weapon power are far more consistent than landing a Pulse Bomb. Do not use Pulse Bomb. Please. (thank you).

For the rest of your items, find the build path you chose in round three and check below.
________________________________________

***“Good Noodle”***

After that, hold onto your blue survival items. Beyond that, the items are flexible - build for the match you’re in. By this point you’re basically a mosquito in Kevlar. Prioritize weapon damage and go bite some ankles.

**Core Items:** [Vanadium Injection](item_57953fbc-11ff-4e92-9928-fc59b7be668f); [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c); [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09) (or [Reinforced Titanium](item_8ebaa7db-aedf-48ed-adc1-318cb46a3214)).

**New Items:** Prioritize weapon damage above all else.
________________________________________

***“LowElo, I Think We’re Gonna Have to Kill This Guy”***

After a full round with [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182) and [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66), you should have a good idea of how effective you’re being - and where you’re falling short. This is where we start to build to cover that gap.
Their Lucio has 150+ armor because he wasn’t annoying enough already, scurrying like a caffeinated roach with a JBL strapped to his back, blasting copyright-free lo-fi EDM and you’re not getting through it quickly enough? Let’s upgrade [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66) to [Codebreaker](item_caa96c7e-655f-4d03-9bd9-0f41937fec27). After that, pump what you can into weapon power and pray for a DC. (*It won’t happen, but visualizing it might lower your blood pressure.*)

If you’re still struggling to stay alive and can’t redirect your focus elsewhere (like DPS picks or tank harassment), go ahead and add some survivability with [Overdrive Core](item_a2a8dba1-5f2f-4da1-9445-b08f49162121). We’re picking this up here instead of [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c) because of the 10% weapon damage boost. The trade-off is that it only procs once per life, but between that and your recall, you should be enough of a threat to their backline - no matter how mobile they are - that you can’t be ignored. And that’s the goal here: attention.

**Core Items:** [Vanadium Injection](item_57953fbc-11ff-4e92-9928-fc59b7be668f); [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182); [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66).

**New Items:** Upgrade [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66) to [Codebreaker](item_caa96c7e-655f-4d03-9bd9-0f41937fec27) if you’re struggling against armor-stacking supports (looking at you, Lucio). If you’re dying too quickly to capitalize on pressure, add [Overdrive Core](item_a2a8dba1-5f2f-4da1-9445-b08f49162121) for extra survivability without sacrificing damage. From here, keep stacking weapon power until they can’t ignore you.
________________________________________

***“Nah, He’s Soft-Locking for Sure”***

Still playing “walk back from spawn simulator”? Let’s add [Overdrive Core](item_a2a8dba1-5f2f-4da1-9445-b08f49162121) if you think you can get away with the once-per-life get-out-of-jail-free card. This will give you a little more survivability without sacrificing weapon power.

If you need something more consistent and can afford it, grab [Nebula Conduit](item_476b7040-54c9-4f0c-8283-b4407f6809f8). Use any remaining Stadium Cash on anything that increases your threat level - weapon power is the priority.

**Core Items:** [Vanadium Injection](item_57953fbc-11ff-4e92-9928-fc59b7be668f); [Auto Recall](item_ae3dbebf-c306-4408-b698-6f666ace0a7c); [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c); [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09).

**New Items: [Overdrive Core](item_a2a8dba1-5f2f-4da1-9445-b08f49162121)** if you can get away with the once-per-life passive, or [Nebula Conduit](item_476b7040-54c9-4f0c-8283-b4407f6809f8) if you prefer something more consistent. Fill any remaining slots with weapon damage-focused items — we’re going for threat level, not subtlety.
________________________________________

***“Pharmerc-udical Solutions”***

If you’re struggling to turn these F-16s into United 93s, it’s because they’ve mistaken altitude for safety – *time to prove that wrong*. Add [Aerial Distresser](item_0fcb9020-c729-49b9-b398-3223797b6204) outright if you can. Between this and [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182) proccing off any of the absurd spread of buckshot you’re unloading at an increasingly rapid pace, you should be drawing all their attention.

If you can’t afford [Aerial Distresser](item_0fcb9020-c729-49b9-b398-3223797b6204), sell [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182) and replace it. If you still can’t afford it *even after selling Beacon…* what are we doing, man? We’re better than this. I still believe in you, chief. So for now, prioritize weapon damage - [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66) is typically a great low-cost alternative against those Pharahs with big shield pools.

**Core Items:** [Vanadium Injection](item_57953fbc-11ff-4e92-9928-fc59b7be668f); [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182) (replace if necessary); [Aerial Distresser](item_0fcb9020-c729-49b9-b398-3223797b6204).

**New Items:** If you can’t afford [Aerial Distresser](item_0fcb9020-c729-49b9-b398-3223797b6204), sell [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182) and replace it. If that’s still out of reach, focus on [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66) or other weapon power options to boost your threat level against airborne targets. The goal here is to punish altitude with overwhelming force - make them regret ever leaving the ground.
________________________________________

And don’t forget - keep those optional items and their notes in mind as you go. They can make the difference depending on the match.

rounds.notes:
Round five is where this build actually comes alive. The training wheels are off, the leash is gone (Don’t worry - you’re ready), and it would be a safe bet to say the in-fighting has already started in the enemy team chat. Your third power here is what transforms you from “annoying problem” into a *malignant presence* they can’t play around.
________________________________________

***“Good Noodle”***

[Auto Recall](item_ae3dbebf-c306-4408-b698-6f666ace0a7c) – At this stage, we’re not picking it because we need it - we’re picking it because nothing breaks morale quite like watching someone burn every cooldown trying to finally put you down, only for you to zip back in time like *“lol, try again.”* You’ll live longer, obviously, but more importantly, you’ll live longer *rent-free* in their heads. Think of this as going from “irritating” to “actively rewriting their definition of futility.” Digital or not, this is war - and war is won in the mind.

**Core Items:** [Vanadium Injection](item_57953fbc-11ff-4e92-9928-fc59b7be668f); [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c); [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09) (or [Reinforced Titanium](item_8ebaa7db-aedf-48ed-adc1-318cb46a3214)); [Vishkar Condensor](item_086a91da-b65d-4047-8fc7-28a992078b1d).

**New Items:** We’re grabbing [Volskaya Ordnance](item_396c0970-daa8-47e3-8049-e65f03fe5cec) - the attack speed and bonus weapon power scaling with enemy health means that supports who thought they were safe by stacking survivability will learn otherwise. This item is situational, though, so pivot as needed. Fighting heavy armor? Grab [Codebreaker](item_caa96c7e-655f-4d03-9bd9-0f41937fec27). Getting walked down by a Reaper who thinks W-key shotguns make him unstoppable? Pick up [Weapon Jammer](item_72386db6-753e-413d-aa2a-f1389842f47f). You’re going to live and die by how well you read enemy builds and morph into whatever is most annoying.
________________________________________

***“LowElo, I Think We’re Gonna Have to Kill This Guy”***

[Timelapse](item_20d43db5-d2ad-47e9-b32f-82d8eca006ce) – This is where we start writing tragedy. All those supports who sprint for their lives the second they see you? Not anymore, they don’t. It’s not enough to be hard to kill - we’re here to be impossible to escape. They’ll try repositioning. They’ll try peeling. They’ll even start playing closer together, clinging to one another for safety like penguins in a blizzard. And none of it will matter. ***You are inevitable.***

**Core Items:** [Codebreaker](item_caa96c7e-655f-4d03-9bd9-0f41937fec27); [Aerial Distresser](item_0fcb9020-c729-49b9-b398-3223797b6204); [Overdrive Core](item_a2a8dba1-5f2f-4da1-9445-b08f49162121); [Aftermarket Firing Pin](item_2485b212-b286-42d0-a2bd-20eb4396b054).

**New Items:** If survivability is still an issue, add [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c). If you’re thriving and just want to make their suffering worse, grab [Booster Jets](item_a291de85-b6d9-43cf-b5da-f3184a156f48) and pump even more damage into the nightmare.
________________________________________

***“Nah, He’s Soft-Locking for Sure”***

[T.Racer](item_996e13d5-9521-4312-944f-d672f528776b) – This isn’t just mobility - it’s psychological sabotage. Their hitscans have spent four rounds training their muscle memory for where you should be. Now? You’re not there. Every shot they take will feel off. Every duel they lose will feel like it wasn’t their fault. And deep down, they’ll start to wonder if maybe they’re just bad. It’s not enough to outplay them - we want them *questioning their worth as a person.*

**Core Items:** [Crusader Hydraulics](item_b64cee07-ca32-405d-987e-868b415bbc09); [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c); [Overdrive Core](item_a2a8dba1-5f2f-4da1-9445-b08f49162121) (or [Nebula Conduit](item_476b7040-54c9-4f0c-8283-b4407f6809f8)).

**New Items:** [Eye of the Spider](item_5e644a79-cf6e-4196-8d0a-232f75004643), [Codebreaker](item_caa96c7e-655f-4d03-9bd9-0f41937fec27), or [Talon Modification Module](item_c0ca1795-a3ea-4dc9-ae17-f34122574b3a) — anything that pushes weapon power as high as possible. If you’re still struggling to stay alive and already have either [Overdrive Core](item_a2a8dba1-5f2f-4da1-9445-b08f49162121) or [Nebula Conduit](item_476b7040-54c9-4f0c-8283-b4407f6809f8), pick up whichever one you’re missing.
________________________________________

***“Pharmerc-udical Solutions”***

•	[Timelapse](item_20d43db5-d2ad-47e9-b32f-82d8eca006ce) – If things are going well, this is your power spike. You’ll melt airborne targets before they even realize they’re being focused.

•	[Auto Recall](item_ae3dbebf-c306-4408-b698-6f666ace0a7c) – If things aren’t going well, this is your lifeline. Survival isn’t just about staying alive — it’s about sticking around long enough to make them wish they’d uninstalled.

**Core Items:** [Aerial Distresser](item_0fcb9020-c729-49b9-b398-3223797b6204); [Stratosphere Beacon](item_15bf2dc7-5161-47b0-929b-17cbb1d54182); [Divine Intervention](item_b5148b7f-8529-4b1b-a90c-5d7cf13f8f0c); [Shieldbuster](item_9ee1f150-537d-40b9-b975-7820fb1c6a66).

**New Items:** If you need more survivability, grab [Overdrive Core](item_a2a8dba1-5f2f-4da1-9445-b08f49162121). If they’re stacking shields over armor, [Volskaya Ordnance](item_396c0970-daa8-47e3-8049-e65f03fe5cec) is your pick. If they’re stacking armor, [Codebreaker](item_caa96c7e-655f-4d03-9bd9-0f41937fec27) is the answer. Unless you absolutely need survivability, the name of the game here is damage and efficiency. If you’re short on Stadium Cash, sell any non-core items to free up funds, or pick up a blue item with the mindset of turning up your damage output.
________________________________________

At this point in the game, your job isn’t just to win - it’s to *demoralize*. The longer you’re alive, the more they tilt. The more they tilt, the worse they play. And the worse they play, the more they feed into the endless cycle of suffering you’re creating.

rounds.notes:
We’re still here? Well, it can’t be you (that wouldn’t be a very DPS mindset), so I can’t believe your:  

a.) Tank  
b.) Other DPS  
c.) Support  
d.) Internet Service Provider  

…is throwing this hard. Don’t crash out (yet) - we can still pull this off. We’re the cavalry, after all.  

Late game, it’s tougher to build strictly by the book - ***rounds 6 and 7 are where boys become men, girls become women, and they’s become them’s.*** Paying attention to enemy builds is the difference between dragging your team kicking and screaming to a Victory screen, or staring at that Defeat screen, reflecting on the choices that landed you here instead of just queueing Mystery Heroes.

Anything past round 5 is fair game for tweaking this build. I promise I won’t be that mad. All you need right now are deep breaths, happy thoughts, and a little murderous intent. Go get ’em, champ.

At this point, all four builds are going to be focused on one thing: damage. Because of that, you’re only going to see one section below for rounds six and seven. I know - change is scary. And yes, it might look like I’m just getting lazy here, but:  

A.) I *am* getting lazy.  
B.) By this point, your core build is already complete, and additional items can vary wildly because the game and your enemies can vary wildly. If I could build a path to round 7 that predicted the exact build of that hard-stuck Pharah you’re up against, I’d be playing the lottery and not writing build guides. But the wisdom you’ve gained over the probably 25 minutes leading up to this round? That’s what’s going to carry you to the win. (Well, that and a few final items - I’m just saying, don’t follow this blindly.)

---

***“All Builds”***  

We’re already strong, but let’s add one final twist of the knife: [Underworld Quickloader](item_dc8e93b1-a561-4007-bfdc-42839f612d01). By now, your ammo reserves are probably emptier than their emotional stability, and Quickloader patches that hole by cranking your reload speed up to absurd levels just for continuing to play the way you already are. You shoot, you reload, you shoot again - a relentless, suffocating loop that, fun fact, technically puts you in violation of Additional Protocol I, Article 51 of the Geneva Conventions. All that to say, if your god complex hasn’t kicked in yet, don’t worry – it’s about to. And as if that wasn’t enough, Quickloader throws in a healthy chunk of bonus weapon power, pushing your pressure from “annoying” to “inescapable.”  

If you can’t afford Quickloader without selling one of your core items, that’s fine - just fill the slot with one of the optional picks or any high-damage option. ([Codebreaker](item_caa96c7e-655f-4d03-9bd9-0f41937fec27) is always a solid fallback, even if the enemy team doesn’t have much armor. Think of it as the blunt instrument approach: if finesse isn’t working, start swinging harder.)

rounds.notes:
Round seven. Wow. Look at us. ***Hey***, look at us. Who would’ve thought? (Not me.)  
I don’t know how this game has gone. I don’t know what in your life has led you here. I don’t know what possessed you to pick up the pulse pistols and never look back. But I do know this: this is your “Miracle on Ice” moment - except not on ice, not necessarily a miracle... honestly more of an intentional harassment campaign conducted on pavement. You get the idea. Let’s finish this.  

These are the four powers that two of the four build paths should end up with by round seven (the exceptions being ***“Pharmerc-udical Solutions,”*** which picks up [Bullet Time](item_6840382c-ae92-491a-b70c-b49f3a76003a), and ***“LowElo, I Think We’re Gonna Have to Kill This Guy,”*** which picks up [Foresight](item_f4163ce1-8f80-43ca-85d4-39812084400f)). For those walking anti-air cannons and support slayers, pick whichever of the following four you’re missing based on your needs this round:  

• [Quantum Clip](item_3a108115-ec6e-4b98-8074-1b015cf535f1)  
• [T.Racer](item_996e13d5-9521-4312-944f-d672f528776b)  
• [Auto Recall](item_ae3dbebf-c306-4408-b698-6f666ace0a7c)  
• [Timelapse](item_20d43db5-d2ad-47e9-b32f-82d8eca006ce)  

The playstyle doesn’t change: don’t frontline unless it’s absolutely necessary. But let’s be real - if we’re in round seven, your frontliners probably aren’t front lining anyway (and it can’t be you, because that’s not a very DPS mindset). Blink, empty a clip, blink, empty a clip, blink, empty a clip, recall when low, rinse, repeat, and keep going for as long as humanly possible. And trust me - by now you’re less of a hero and more of an intangible sleep paralysis demon with fully automatic shotguns and a British accent, and that “as long as humanly possible” can be very long.

________________________________________

***“All Builds”***  
We’re already strong, but let’s push things over the edge: [Eye of the Spider](item_3b0e7be5-3d2a-4f5d-8eb8-1659b3c6d687). The name of the game is still damage, but this is where adaptive damage starts to matter. If all five enemies are stacking armor, [Codebreaker](item_caa96c7e-655f-4d03-9bd9-0f41937fec27) might give you more consistent value than Eye of the Spider.  

Beyond that, [Booster Jets](item_a291de85-b6d9-43cf-b5da-f3184a156f48) is a personal favorite - especially against heroes who love to vanish mid-fight (Moira, Kiriko, Tracer, Reaper, D.Va). It lets you dump as much damage as possible before they can run away and regret their life choices.  

The only blue item likely still lingering in your build is your original survival pick. If you’ve got the Stadium Cash to spare, now’s the time to swap it out - grab [Nebula Conduit](item_476b7040-54c9-4f0c-8283-b4407f6809f8) if you’re worried about an enemy powerspike, or [Phantasmic Flux](item_5e644a79-cf6e-4196-8d0a-232f75004643) if you want to keep scaling like the terrifying damage engine you’ve become.

________________________________________

***Win or lose, I’m proud of you.***

And don’t forget the DPS creed: 
 
You played perfectly.  
Your teammates? Bots.  
The enemy team? Boosted.  
The matchmaker? A sentient Excel sheet running on a PC powered by Windows Vista and its only purpose in this cruel, uncaring world is to ruin your SR.  

God speed.
